method: read-only session against the LIVE database; pg_proc/pg_policies catalog, never a migration file
purpose: Evidence for the A3 classifier refinement (cc-fleet-health's pen): a PUBLIC/anon EXECUTE grant that RLS DEPENDS ON is not the same defect as a sloppy grant.
rule_under_test: Reclassify a PUBLIC/anon-EXECUTE SECDEF fn out of FAIL only if BOTH hold: (1) it is referenced in an RLS policy expression, AND (2) it is caller-scoped (derives from auth.uid(), returns empty for anon). Condition (1) alone is NOT sufficient.
caveats: policy_refs uses a LIKE substring match on proname; distinctive here, but tighten (word-boundary regex or pg_depend) if this becomes a standing classifier.
Condition (2) rests on at-source reads of each function body — see secdef-12-caller-vs-target-assessment.md.
A verification is true at an instant: this reflects the catalog at generated_at_utc.

result_summary.partition: clean — the RLS-load-bearing set is exactly the 8 auth_user_*; the unreferenced set is exactly donation_category_in_use + the 2 trigger fns
